title: INNER JOIN
definition:
Combines rows from two views by returning only the records that have matching values in both views.
If no match exists, the row is excluded from the result.
For example, only products that have a valid CategoryID matching an existing category will be returned.

title: LEFT JOIN
definition:
Combines rows from two views by returning all records from the left view and the matching records from the right view.
If no match is found, the right-side columns return null.
This allows you to identify missing relationships, such as customers who have not placed any orders by filtering where the joined column is null.

title: RIGHT JOIN
definition:
Combines rows from two views by returning all records from the right view and the matching records from the left view.
If no match is found, the left-side columns return null.
This allows you to retrieve all records from the right table (for example, all employees), even if they are not associated with any records in the left table (orders).

title: MULTIPLE JOIN
definition:
Allows combining data from more than two views by applying multiple JOIN operations in a single query.
Each join links the main view to another related view using its own condition.
This makes it possible to retrieve related data from several tables at once.
